sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case M06: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 440x440x224 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case M06 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(440, 440, 224) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: myxoid soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).

I'll now check the sagittal plane through this lesion, starting with axial 100 to establish reference marks.

content.thinking:
I'm noticing the coronal view is zoomed oddly, and the mask covers axial slices 73–138, but the bright lesion area actually extends lower, down to around axial 45 laterally in the posterior left thigh, with a moderately bright region visible outside the mask boundary on the coronal image.

I'm trying to figure out whether that lower tail at axial slices 51-78 is actually part of the tumor or something separate — it's quite bright at 78, moderate at 64, and shows as a bright spot posterolaterally at 51. I want to check a coronal or sagittal sheet through the lesion, particularly around coronal index 160, to get a better sense of the anterior-posterior extent.

content.text: sheet coronal 130–185/440 (8 slices) | v1 | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm trying to work out the orientation of the coronal slices, noting that higher coronal indices seem to correspond to more anterior positions, with the lesion itself situated posteriorly. Around coronal 161-177, I notice a moderately bright, heterogeneous structure inferolateral to the main mass, and I'm trying to determine whether this represents a distinct lesion or an extension of the primary one.

I'm wondering whether this bright tail could be tumor extending along the sciatic nerve, muscle edema, or a separate myxoid lesion. It seems contiguous with the main mass at coronal 161 but shows a gap at 169, so I want to cross-reference this against axial slices 78 and 64 to get a clearer picture of that posterolateral elongated structure.

content.text: axial 80/224 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At slice 80, the bright area extends laterally from the medial mass, sharing the same striated texture, suggesting tumor extension along the muscle — possibly an intramuscular myxoma or myxoid liposarcoma in the gluteus maximus/hamstring region. The lateral feathery brightness could represent peritumoral edema, which is characteristic of myxoid tumors like intramuscular myxoma.

But I also notice on slices 51 and 64 there's a distinct, fairly bright area more inferiorly and laterally that warrants a closer look.

content.text: axial 80/224 | crop marks | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial slice 80, the lateral extension shares the same bright, septated character as the medial portion and appears contiguous with it, even though the mask only covers the medial half there. The intensities at the lateral points are comparably bright to the lower-intensity medial regions, so I'm leaning toward this lateral extension also being tumor.

Checking additional slices — axial 64, 51, and 37 show progressively smaller bright spots laterally, and the coronal images (169-177) reveal a separate elongated, moderately bright structure extending inferolaterally. This looks like a fusiform extension in the subcutaneous/gluteal region rather than deeper structures like the sciatic nerve. Since the rule is to include any extension contiguous with the mass, I'll add positive points at these lateral locations.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 108.7 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 32–139, coronal 136–182, sagittal 97–220 | change +42.0 mL / -0.1 mL | tool calls 8/40, prompts 2/15 | point add (2 mark(s)) | image: axial 91, coronal 159, sagittal 168 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
I'm puzzling over the extended range now—sagittal 97–220 is much larger than the original 154–218, which makes me question the orientation and which direction the lesion actually extends toward relative to patient left versus image right.

I should cross-check with the coronal 159 image and look at coronal 170 with the outline overlaid to confirm the inferolateral tail portion of the mass.

content.thinking: The coronal image appears squashed given the aspect ratio mismatch, but the inferolateral tail region looks heterogeneous and moderately bright, which fits with a tumor component like myxoid liposarcoma, though it could just be another lobule — I'll keep this interpretation for now. I should double-check the sagittal extent around slice 97, since that seems too far out, by reviewing the mask on a sagittal view or the corresponding axial slices.

content.text: sheet sagittal 95–225/440 (12 slices) | v2 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
Tracing the lesion tail across sagittal slices, it seems to extend as a moderately bright, continuous tubular structure through the posterior subcutaneous thigh region. I'm trying to figure out whether this tail represents part of the tumor itself or a separate structure entirely.

Given the sharp, lobulated margins seen in sagittal 119-142, this looks more like true tumor extension rather than feathery edema signal. Now I want to verify the superior and medial extent of the mask against the actual mass boundaries by checking specific axial slices and running segmentation candidates to confirm full coverage.

content.text: axial 48/224 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: I'm comparing the mask boundaries at axial slice 48 against the bright region location in the clean image, checking whether the mask fully covers that bright area after accounting for the coordinate offset between the two panels. It looks like the bright region extends a bit beyond the mask boundaries rather than being fully contained within it.

content.text: axial 48/224 | crop marks | marks fine | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 16/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
At axial 48, the bright region in the clean panel aligns with the mask boundary at the offset coordinates, with the mask largely covering the brighter part while the medial edge remains faintly visible — this looks like ill-defined, feathery hyperintensity in muscle, possibly edema.

A similar small bright spot appears at axial 37 in the left posterior thigh, with mask coverage extending to axial 32. I'm now weighing whether the tail-like extension represents tumor or edema — the main mass sits in the gluteal/upper posterior thigh region, and the tail's inferolateral orientation matches the fiber direction of gluteus maximus, suggesting either tumor infiltrating along those fibers or simple muscular edema. The streaky, striated signal pattern at axial 80 could fit either an infiltrating myxoid tumor with peritumoral edema or isolated edema within the muscle.

Peritumoral edema is a recognized feature of these lesions in up to 80% of cases, and the tail's moderate intensity at axial 80, heterogeneous texture on coronal 170, but fairly well-defined lobular shape on sagittal 119-142 makes this ambiguous. Since annotators usually segment only the tumor itself rather than surrounding edema, I want to zoom into sagittal 125 to better judge the tail's intensity and margins before deciding.

content.text: coronal 165/440 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
I'm noting that the tail region looks more edematous and ill-defined compared to the well-circumscribed, very bright main mass, which makes me weigh myxoid liposarcoma against intramuscular myxoma — both can be well-defined and T2-bright, but the myxoma's peritumoral edema and fat rim could explain this contiguous tail-like extension.

But then I reconsider myxofibrosarcoma, which classically shows a "tail sign" — infiltrative tumor extension along fascial planes that is actually tumor, not just edema — and the instructions' emphasis on including any contiguous extension along fascia or between muscles strongly suggests I should keep that tail as part of the lesion. I also note a thin bright band extending superomedially from the mass on the coronal image, which appears contiguous and should likewise be included.

I'm checking that the mask fully captures the tail's inferior end and the faint lower periphery of the main mass on the clean coronal panel, and both look adequately covered by the boundary. Now I want to move to the sagittal view to verify the anterior and posterior extent of the mass and tail together.

content.thinking: It's hard to tell much at this zoom level, so I'll move on and check the overall result in a final review.

arguments.reason: Main bright myxoid mass plus contiguous inferolateral tail included.

The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. content.thinking: I should keep my answer brief and to the point.

content.text:
I saved the mask for case M06 (version v2), with medium confidence. The main open question is whether a tail of signal running from the mass belongs to the tumor.

**What's in the mask:** 108.7 mL in one connected piece, covering axial slices 32–139, coronal 136–182 and sagittal 97–220. It used 20 of the 40 tool calls and 2 of the 15 model prompts.

- **Main mass:** a sharply bounded, very bright, lobulated mass in the posterior left buttock and upper thigh. One click inside it captured it, and the outline follows its edge in all three planes.
- **Tail:** a less bright, uneven band runs from the mass down and outward along the line of the buttock muscle, reaching about axial slice 32. A second prompt added it, which accounts for about 42 mL of the total.

**Why medium confidence:** I kept the tail because it joins the mass directly and your instructions say to include extensions along fascia or between muscles. Myxoid tumors such as myxofibrosarcoma can also spread along fascia in this way. But the tail is clearly dimmer, less sharply bounded and streaky, so it could instead be fluid (edema) in the muscle around the tumor. If the reference outline covers only the main mass, this mask is about 40 mL too large.

**Checks:**
- The final review slices just past each end of the mask showed no lesion left out.
- None of the four automatic suggestions were added. Two were rings of normal tissue around the mask, and two were tiny specks well away from it.
- The bright structures at the front of the pelvis, in the scrotum and bladder, are normal anatomy and were left out.
